To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the composition of the species in bryophytes is affected by the substrate, ecological amplitude, and type of strategy.

the composition of the moss component of secondary communities is determined by the type of life strategy, substrate confinement, and ecological amplitude in relation with the factors of temperature and humidity.
the bryophytic component of the forest ecosystems of the Bashkir Ural Region is very sensitive to clear felling, especially in terms of its epiphytic component.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the bryophytes in the course of the secondary succession in the forest communities of the Bashkirian Cis-Ural region.
the influence of the clear felling of forests in the Bashkir Cisa-Ural on the composition and structure of the bryoflora.
the change in the species composition of bryophytes during the succession in the secondary aspen forest and the role of the moss layer in the process of regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the clear fellings have a negative effect on the moss component of broad-leaved forests of the Bashkortostan Cis-Ural region.
the composition of the moss flora of the secondary aspen stands in the Bashkir Ciso-Ural region is significantly different from the moss flora of natural broad-leaved forests.
the bryophytic component of the forest ecosystems of the Cis-Ural is characterized by a high degree of vulnerability to the consequences of clear felling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bryophytic component of the secondary forests of the Bashkortostan Cis-Ural region is characterized by low species diversity.

the bryophytic component of the secondary aspen forest is characterized by a high degree of instability, which is due to the low constancy of species of the bryoflora of the nemoral type and a high degree of vulnerability of the species of this group.

the bryophytic vegetation of the secondary forest communities that form in the process of the regeneration of the clear-felled areas of the elm—maple—linden forest is significantly different from the bryophytic vegetation of the original forest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the species composition of bryophytes in secondary forests is determined by the type of felling, which is reflected in the composition of species, and the type of forest that is being formed.
the bryophytic component of the secondary forest is not fully reconstituted in the process of secondary succession, and its species composition is not identical to the original forest.

the composition of the epiphytic mosses in the secondary forests is determined by the species composition of their substrates, while that of the ground mosses is determined by the composition of the soil and the degree of its development.
